paper.title_en: Coupling-Response Thermodynamic Density of States for Bosonic Working Media
paper.abstract_en: We introduce an operational thermodynamic density of states (TDOS), $\mathcal{G}_λ=(\partial S/\partialλ)_{T,μ}$, to characterize bosonic working media under microscopic spectral control. At fixed chemical potential, the response is strictly driven by the structural density of states, yielding the exact scaling law $\mathcal{G}_λ=-(d/α)S/λ$ for homogeneous spectra $ε(k)=Δ+λk^α$, while coupling-dependent gaps generate edge terms only for finite boundary weight. Under a fixed-particle constraint, a secondary chemical-potential redistribution channel emerges. Exact solutions for quadratic bands and harmonic traps demonstrate that spatial dimensionality dictates whether this constrained TDOS exhibits a jump discontinuity or remains continuous across the Bose--Einstein condensation threshold. For pure scale control, the response maps exactly to the heat capacity, $λ\mathcal{G}_λ^{(N)}=-C_N$. This framework is applied to evaluate reversible work in Stirling cycles and to identify observables in magnonic platforms, contrasting global spectral edges with topological Dirac gaps in honeycomb ferromagnets.
